Primary human knee chondrocytes, control vs CAVIN1 knockout; no senescence inducer was applied and no sample is described as senescent or proliferating. Culture is inferred from the knockout of extracted chondrocytes.

Senescence is inferred from the series text (cells 'made senescent by genotoxicity in vitro' with bleomycin); no senescence marker is reported in the fields. BLEO/PQQ samples are excluded because PQQ is a senomorphic perturbation added to senescent cells.

All three samples in this dataset are bleomycin-treated PSC27 cells further exposed to melatonin (a senotherapeutic test), so none is a plain senescent or control sample. The CTRL and BLEO samples that the design says were re-used are in another series (GSE264076) and not here.

All samples in this dataset are day 3 of 4-OHT treatment, the early stress-response phase before SASP; the series names no day-3 sample as senescent, so no sample is labelled senescent. Day 8 samples named in the design are not in this dataset.

All samples are human lung tissue (paraffin slides, laser-captured LAM nodules, rest of lung, transplant lung), not cultured cells; no senescence was induced in these samples. Senescence is only inferred from p16/p21 and SenMayo in the study text.

Senescence here is induced by PTBP1 shRNA knockdown in HFF cells (three shRNAs); the series says knockdown induced senescence-associated phenotypes, without naming the assay. The source_name 'Epithelial tissue' conflicts with the HFF fibroblast cell line, and the overall design only describes qRT-PCR.

confirmation_stated: p16INK4A expression (diffuse p16INK4A expression in around 40% of patients, showing senescence phenotype)
note: All samples are surgically removed human glioblastoma tissue or perilesional normal brain, not cultured cells, and no senescence was induced. p16INK4A-high/low is a tumour classification, not a senescence induction.

confirmation_stated: Multiparametric flow cytometry showing CD28-CD57+ senescent cells; telomere shortening by RT-PCR and telomere dysfunction by IF-FISH; DDR activation
note: Primary peripheral blood CD8+ T cells from axial spondyloarthritis patients, split into migrated and not migrated in a transwell assay. No senescence was induced in culture, and the migrated subset is only described as enriched in senescent-phenotype cells.

Each sample pools several time points (0-24 h) and four treatment groups (control, 18β-GA, IL6, IL6+GA), so the samples are not separable into plain senescent and control conditions. No senescence marker is reported in the summary.
Only basal controls and 8 h post-15 Gy irradiation samples are in this dataset; 8 h is too early for senescence, so no sample is senescent. Controls are not stated to be proliferating or quiescent.

confirmation_stated: β-galactosidase (Bgal) staining assessed after 6 days; Bgal positive and negative cells sorted
note: Senescent and non-senescent samples are both stretched A549 cells, sorted by Bgal staining; the non-senescent ones are Bgal-negative stretched cells, not unstretched controls. The inducer, mechanical stretch, is classed as 'other'.

confirmation_stated: Beta-galactosidase (Bgal) staining after 6 days; Bgal-positive cells were sorted for RNA-seq
note: All samples are Bgal-positive sorted A549 cells (stretch or doxorubicin); no non-senescent control in this dataset. Time is 24 h treatment followed by 6 days before Bgal assessment.

The profiled cells are MRC5 fibroblasts treated with conditioned media from A549 cells. The series says stretch does not induce senescence in fibroblasts, so the dataset has no senescent sample. The stretch samples show fibroblast activation by paracrine signals, not senescence.

SuperSeries with no summary text; labels rest on sample descriptions. A549 stretch samples are B-gal sorted (positive vs negative) from the same stretched culture. Doxorubicin A549 samples carry no senescence statement, so they are unclear. MRC5 samples are fibroblasts given A549 conditioned medium, not a senescence induction.

RNA-seq compares CSRNP1 overexpression with empty-vector lentivirus in normal vaginal fibroblasts for 48 h. No senescence inducer was applied and no sample is described as senescent. The senescence markers p21 and γ-H2Ax in the summary come from separate etoposide experiments.

Senescent samples are replicative senescent LF1 cells kept in the senescent state for 3-4 months; the series states no separate confirmation assay. Quiescent and proliferating samples are both controls.

The UVB-resistant samples are a subpopulation that resisted UVB-induced premature senescence and sits between young and senescent cells, so they are labelled excluded. The senescent samples are induced by gamma-irradiation, not UVB.

confirmation_stated: Increased p16INK4a, p21CIP1, senescence-associated β-galactosidase (Saβgal), γH2AX, and proliferative arrest (stated for senescent cells in the summary)
note: All samples are irradiated senescent preadipocytes. DMSO samples are the total senescent population (vehicle). Dasatinib samples are the senolytic-resistant survivors and are excluded. There are no non-senescent controls.

The fields only imply YAP1-induced senescence (summary: HPV prevents YAP1-induced senescence); no senescence marker is given for these samples, only YAP1 expression by RT-PCR/Western. YAPS127A labelled senescent on that basis; E6E7 samples are not controls.

Ethanol-treated VL-17A cells (100 mM, 48 h) are compared with untreated cells. The series title suggests senescence, but the fields give no senescence marker and do not say the senescent state was reached, so ethanol samples are unclear and the controls are unclear too.

WJ-MSC GMP manufacturing study (passage 0, 2, 3; low vs high seeding density) with no senescence induction and no senescent condition; senescence is only mentioned as a gene-expression pattern. All samples are labelled excluded.

Acute (3-6 h) auxin depletion of NELF-C in DLD-1 cells with ELOA KO or Tet-ELOA/GFP; no sample is described as senescent (growth arrest only follows long-term depletion, which is not sampled here), so all samples are excluded.

Donor-age comparison of adipose-derived stem cells (young vs old donors); no senescence was induced or confirmed, so no sample is labelled senescent or as a control. Culture of the ADSCs is inferred from the cell type, not stated.

Senescence is induced with inflachromene (ICM, 6 days at most), and the knockdown samples (siSRRM2, siBANF1, siCTCF) are done on the ICM background. The last four samples have cell line names IMR91 to IMR94, which look like labelling errors for IMR90.
Post-mortem human brain tissue (AD vs control) from a spatial transcriptomics study; no senescence induction or senescent condition, so all samples are excluded as not cultured cells.

All samples are acute (3-6 hr) auxin-degron depletions or controls in DLD-1 cells; the series describes long-term growth arrest elsewhere, but no sample here is a senescent condition, so none can be labelled senescent or as a control of one.
All samples are old ADSCs (O-ADSCs); the series never states that they are senescent, so the oe-NC samples are unclear. The oe-HES1 samples are an overexpression perturbation.

Title mentions ATF6α-induced senescence, but the fields name no senescent time point and give no senescence marker. Transient transfection was sampled only at 6 h and 9 h, so all samples are labelled unclear.

Senescence is not directly measured in the described fields; the HRasG12V-only HBEC is taken as the OIS condition from the series text. Twist1wt samples are treated as senescence bypass and Twist1F187G samples as an added perturbation.

Cells are iPSCs and iPSC-derived NPCs from a patient IVNS1ABP mutation, a CRISPR-corrected control and a KO line. The summary says mutant cells show senescence but names no senescent condition or assay for these RNA-seq samples, so all states are unclear.

Time course of ER:RAS(G12V) induction in WI38 with 4-OHT; the series focuses on the first 24 h (commitment to OIS) and does not name the senescent time point or give a senescence assay, so the 144 h (day 6) sample is labelled senescent as the last time point. 2-24 h samples are intermediate; the only control is an EtOH sample at 2 h.

Neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y WDFY3 siRNA knockdown study with no senescence induction and no senescent condition; the growth protocol only mentions discarding cells at passage 15 to prevent senescence. GSM8380954 is titled p19, but its description says p101, so the title may be a typo.

The series only compares control shRNA with DKC1-knockdown WIDR colorectal cancer cells and never states that senescence was reached, so no sample can be labelled senescent or as a control of senescent cells.
FLS were stimulated with recombinant CCN3 (100 ng/mL); the title says CCN3 promotes senescence, but the fields give no senescence measurement or time point, so the state is unclear for all samples.

Time after irradiation is not given in the fields. The summary and design name no measurement of senescence (such as SA-beta-gal), so the senescent label rests on the design's wording 'radiation-induced senescent cells'.

No sample is described as senescent; the study is about rejuvenation by STAT5A knockout. The numbers in titles (8, 50, 80) are not explained in the fields, so they may be passage or age but this is not stated.

All samples are irradiated (20 Gy, day 14); there is no non-irradiated control. sgPRM1 is the control guide, so PRM1 KO samples are the senescent reference; ALIX and TOR1A KO samples are perturbed and excluded.

Only parental MCF7 day 21 is taken as senescent (last time point; the series does not name the senescent time point, and the summary mentions up to 29 days while the design lists up to day 21). All p53KO samples are excluded because the TP53 knockout is an added perturbation and is reported to prevent senescence.

The fields say only that cells were stimulated with doxorubicin; the time point and a senescence readout are not stated, so the doxorubicin samples are labelled unclear. BNIP3 siRNA samples are perturbations and are excluded.

IMR90 carry hTERT and a doxycycline-inducible shRNA (ATG7 or ATG13); only dox- samples are unperturbed controls or senescent samples, while dox+ samples have autophagy knocked down and are excluded. No senescence marker is stated in the series text.

Apigenin-treated bleomycin cells (B_APIG) are excluded as a perturbation that may change the state. The series does not state a senescence marker, but describes bleomycin-induced senescence of PSC27 cells.

confirmation_stated: senescence-associated-beta-gal expression, cell enlargement, lamin B1 downregulation, elevated p21 levels
note: The series does not name which BMP4 time point is senescent; BMP4 samples from 12 days on were labelled senescent and 7 days as intermediate. GSM8424892 and GSM8424893 have a title saying ctrl/navitoclax but a description saying BMP4-DMSO/BMP4-ABT, so their condition is uncertain. Palbociclib and irradiation samples are reference inducers that the series does not describe, so they are unclear.

DPP4 is overexpressed in a chondrocyte line as a candidate senescence regulator; no senescence inducer was applied and no sample is stated to be senescent or proliferating, so the dataset has no senescent condition.

The series text does not mention senescence and gives no senescent condition; all samples are labelled excluded (no senescent condition). The study compares empty vector, DPP4 overexpression and DPP4 overexpression plus 4,5-dicaffeoylquinic acid in C28/I2 chondrocytes.

Senescence is inferred from the series title and summary (nS100A9 triggers hAF senescence). The overall design does not name a senescence marker or the time point at which senescence was reached. The inducer is overexpression of nuclear S100A9, labelled 'other'.
Small RNA (18-30nt) sequencing of miRNAs, two samples only (young vs senescent). The series states senescent cells were passaged 34 times and had ceased growth; no marker assay is given.

Oncogene-induced senescence in IMR90 (inducer not named in the fields beyond 'oncogene-induced'); the time point is not stated. The ACSS2 knockdown samples are excluded as perturbed; the scramble-shRNA samples are the senescent condition.

RNA-seq was done in HEK293T cells, not in hMSCs where the series reports MRG15-depletion senescence; no senescence marker is stated for these cells, so the shMRG samples and their controls are labelled unclear.

The text frames cyclic tensile strain as inducing chondrocyte senescence but states no senescence marker or that the senescent state was reached, so the strained samples and their controls are labelled unclear.

Cancer cell lines (HUCCT1, EGI-1) treated 72 h with decitabine and/or talazoparib; the summary links the combination to senescence/SASP only by transcriptomic and mechanistic claims, with no confirming assay or explicit senescent condition for these RNA-seq samples, so all are labelled unclear.

Every sample received etoposide and there is no untreated control. The fields do not say that senescence was confirmed, so the wild-type samples are unclear. The BMAL1 knockouts are excluded as perturbations. Etoposide duration is given as 24 h (protocol) and 12 h (characteristics).

confirmation_stated: nuclear structure, proliferation, p21 expression, beta-galactosidase activity (listed as experiments evaluating aging features)
note: Senescence is induced by the SLO small-molecule cocktail (6 days) in immortalized HMC3 microglia. The SLO 1/2 dose is not explicitly stated to reach senescence, so it is labelled unclear; the full dose is the senescent condition.

The series describes DOX-persisting proliferating cells and does not state that the cells became senescent, so DOX and untreated samples are labelled unclear. Samples include scRNA-seq and bulk mRNA-seq of HCT116; the shared growth protocol also lists other mouse cells, which do not appear in these samples.

The series is framed around apoptosis and stress response; the only senescence mention is that HUVECs were 'characterized by analysis of typical senescence phenotypes', with no result or assay named. Treated and control samples are therefore labelled unclear.

The text mentions only that HMEC-1 was 'characterized by analysis of typical senescence phenotypes', with no result or assay named. The summary frames the response as apoptosis and stress, so senescence is not confirmed and all samples are labelled unclear.

All six samples are irradiated HK-2 cells (8 Gy, day 7), with NC lentivirus or PRDM16 overexpression. The text never says directly that the irradiated HK-2 cells became senescent, so the NC samples are labelled unclear, and the PRDM16 samples are excluded as a perturbation. There is no unirradiated control.

HMC3 is an SV40-immortalized microglial line; bleomycin-treated cells are described as therapy-induced senescent, but no senescence marker is given in the summary. BLEO/DMY samples are senolytic-treated and excluded.

Timepoints 1-8 are not defined in the fields and the series does not say which timepoint is senescent, so wild-type samples are unclear. hTERT samples are labelled excluded as immortalised derivatives that avoid replicative arrest. Substrate stiffness varies (0.5 kPa to 2.3 GPa).

WI-38 cells were grown on substrates of different stiffness and collected at three unnamed timepoints on the way to replicative arrest. The fields do not say which timepoint or substrate is senescent, so all samples are labelled unclear. Timepoint 3 is missing for the 2 kPa substrate.

All samples are granulosa cells isolated directly from patients' follicular fluid (endometriosis vs male-factor infertility controls), not cultured cells. No senescence was induced in culture, and no senescence assay is given for these bulk samples.

Senescent label for KP4_Ctrl_Folfirinox rests on the series saying FOLFIRINOX induces senescence; no senescence marker is given in the fields. E5 samples are cells that escaped 5 FOLFIRINOX cycles (resistant/escape derivatives), so they are excluded.

Hep3B cancer cells with PD-L1 knockout, comparing nuclear PD-L1 overexpression with vector. No senescence inducer was applied and no sample is described as senescent, so none was labelled senescent or control.

confirmation_stated: growth arrest, increased cell senescence and decreased clonogenicity after sustained panobinostat treatment (assay not specified)
note: Senescence is only one of several reported effects of panobinostat (mainly framed as differentiation therapy) in ATRT tumour cell lines; the summary gives no named senescence assay, so the senescent label for panobinostat samples is weakly supported.

Palbociclib-treated (72 h) LOVO lines are taken as senescent from the series wording; no senescence assay is named in the text. S-CM-treated and palbociclib+erlotinib samples are excluded as additional perturbations; PIK3CA-mutant lines are lentivirally engineered.

Chordoma study of TBXT inhibition; the summary only says T-DARPins 'induced signs of senescence' and does not say a senescent state was reached, so T-DARPin samples and the control DARPin samples are labelled unclear.

The 4OHT + siSMARCA4 samples are excluded because of the knockdown. Sample titles carry codes (1V, 2VM, etc.) that the fields do not explain; they look like replicate labels. No senescence marker is stated in the series text.

Only a gene knockdown (FGF9 shRNA) versus control shRNA in a chondrocyte line; no senescence inducer is applied, and the summary only says FGF9 depletion exacerbates senescence, without naming a senescent condition or assay.

No senescent condition: RPE1 cells with control or TOP2B siRNA; senescence is only mentioned as a comparison in the summary. All samples are excluded; the TOP2B knockdown samples are also a perturbation.

Primary bone marrow HSPCs sorted from SCD and non-SCD patients, not cultured and with no senescence induction. The summary says SCD HSPCs show hallmarks of senescence, but it names no senescent condition, so all samples are excluded as not cultured cells.

All samples are bone marrow HSPCs or LT-HSCs taken directly from SCD patients/mice and non-SCD controls, with no senescence induction in culture. The title suggests premature senescence in SCD, but the fields do not state that the cells are senescent, so all samples are excluded as not cultured cells.

Dataset compares a spontaneously immortalized prostate cancer line (CaB34) with its radioresistant subline (CaB34-CF); no sample is described as senescent or as proliferating/quiescent, so all are excluded. Senescence is only mentioned for NNMT knockdown after irradiation, which is not in these samples.

Senescence is induced by auxin-triggered degradation of UHRF1 and/or DNMT1 in HCT116 cancer cells; the series does not name the senescent time point, so Day 8 (last) is taken as senescent and Days 2 and 6 as intermediate. WT cells given auxin serve as controls; the summary states no senescence assay.

All samples are single-nucleus RNA-seq of internal thoracic artery from CAD patients in a quercetin vs placebo trial, with no senescence induced in culture. Quercetin is described as a senolytic, so the treated samples are also not plain senescent samples.

IMR90-hTERT with Dox-inducible YAP5SA; only the dox- samples are plain controls/senescent, while dox+ samples (YAP5SA expressed) are excluded as perturbations. The summary states no senescence marker assay.
All samples are alisertib-induced senescent A549 cells. Salinomycin-treated samples (a senolytic candidate) are excluded, and no non-senescent control is present.
Sen(IR) samples are the senescent condition; the CTPI2 and UK5099 treated irradiated samples are excluded as drug perturbations (they suppress the SASP). Time after irradiation is not stated.

Study of cancer cell detachment after 2DG, 2DG+metformin or polyHEMA; senescence is not induced or mentioned, so no sample is senescent and all are excluded. Samples include detached, attached and repeatedly selected detached subpopulations.

The samples are SK-MES-1 cancer cells with or without exosomes from IPF fibroblasts, not senescent cells themselves. The dataset has no senescent condition, so none of the samples is labelled senescent or a control.

No senescence was induced or measured; this is a drug-treatment study of healthy primary dermal fibroblasts (alpha-MSH, BMS-470539, itraconazole vs vehicle). All samples are labelled excluded because the dataset has no senescent condition.

Senescence is only mentioned in the summary as a consequence of METTL3 depletion (premature senescence) with no named time point; I treated the KO (wo DOX) P2/P3 samples as senescent. Titles say P1 but the treatment field says P2 for the 'P1' samples, so they are unclear. ActD samples and HUES8 STM2457/DMSO samples are not clearly tied to a senescent state.

confirmation_stated: increased oxidative stress, DNA damage (pH2AX), cellular senescence (p16) and decreased cell proliferation in DOXO-treated hCardioids
note: Doxorubicin-treated organoids are the senescent condition; D+Q (senolytic) samples are excluded. The iPSC and day 8 differentiation samples are developmental reference samples, not matched controls, and are excluded.

Senescence here is attributed to RUNX2 or NCOR1 siRNA depletion in SAOS2 cells (48 h); the fields name no senescence assay and do not say HDAC3 siRNA induces senescence, so HDAC3 knockdown samples and their controls are unclear.

Replicative senescence in LF1 lung fibroblasts; both early (1 month after replicative exhaustion) and late (4 months) senescence are described as senescent states, and the proliferating early-passage cells are the control. No senescence marker measurement is stated in the series text.
Only a 5-hour DMSO vs ETC-501 (MNK inhibitor) comparison in LN229 and T98G; no TMZ treatment or senescent condition is in this dataset, so no sample is labelled senescent or as a control.

High glucose is not stated to have produced senescence in these podocytes, and no senescence marker is given, so high-glucose samples are labelled unclear and their controls unclear. GPR124-overexpression samples are excluded as perturbations; the Gpr125/Gpr126 and 49h/50h entries look like typos.

Overall design says RNA-seq was done on cartilage tissue from 3 OA patients and 3 healthy individuals, although the source field says primary chondrocytes. These are not cultured cells and no senescence was induced or confirmed in the samples.

All samples are irradiated WI-38 cells at day 5; the control-media group is treated as the senescent condition and the hTSC secretome group is excluded as a perturbation aimed at suppressing SASP. The series gives no non-irradiated control and states no senescence marker, only 'senescent WI-38 cells'.
The series states that OIS cells were harvested one week after 4-OHT; DMSO samples are inferred as vehicle controls from the sample titles. No senescence marker assay is stated.

The human ARPE19 samples are cultured cells (plastic control, 1.5 kPa soft hydrogel as the adhesion-impaired senescence model, YAP-HA overexpression on 1.5 kPa); the mouse samples are RPE from old mice with or without TRULI and are not cultured cells. The summary does not name a measurement confirming senescence, and the 1.5 kPa senescent label rests on the summary statement that impaired adhesion induces senescence.

confirmation_stated: Relative senescence below 5% at young passage and 15% to 20% at older passage (assay not named)
note: Old passages have only 15-20% senescent cells, so the series does not state that a senescent state was reached; old and young samples are labelled unclear. HGPS (LMNA c.1824C>T) strains are patient-derived, and the study is miRNA sequencing.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal staining (and secretory protein profiles by mass spectrometry)
note: All 12 samples are doxorubicin-treated IMR-90 (100 or 250 nM) on plastic or 2 kPa hydrogel; no control samples are in this dataset. The shared treatment text says μM but the sample titles say nM.

The dataset compares TMZ-resistant derivatives with sensitive parental glioblastoma lines. Resistant lines are post-senescence escapers (bypass), and no sample is labelled senescent, so the sensitive lines have no senescent counterpart.

The series text does not state that FK866 (NAMPT inhibitor, NAD+ depletion) produced senescence, so no sample is labelled senescent. Non-treated cells are unclear because their comparison condition is unclear. The FK866 + NAD liposome sample is excluded because the liposome is an added perturbation.

Primary CD4 T cells from patients with musculoskeletal complaints, activated with anti-CD3 for 48 h; the series has no senescence induction, senescent condition or control, so all samples are excluded.

All samples are patient-derived xenograft tumours from mice treated in vivo with vehicle, BLU-222, palbociclib or both; no senescent condition is defined and senescence is only mentioned as an RNA-seq pathway result. Labels for all samples are therefore excluded as not cultured cells.
Senescence is induced by shRNA knockdown of PML (inducer classed as other); the summary names the senescence phenotype of PML-deficient cells but gives no time point or specific assay.

Series text is only a SuperSeries stub; senescent state is taken from the treatment field 'ICM inducing senescence' (up to 6 days ICM). Samples GSM8607128-31 have cell line names IMR91-IMR94 in the fields, apparently mislabels of IMR90 (titles say IMR90). Knockdown samples are excluded as perturbations.

BJ fibroblasts treated 48 h with GSSG or control liposome; the series does not describe any sample as senescent (senescence is not induced here), so no senescent condition is present. Samples are labelled excluded.
HEK293T splicing study (ZNF207 knockdown) with no senescence induction or senescent condition; all samples are labelled excluded because the dataset has no senescent sample.
HEK293T splicing study (ZNF207 knockdown/rescue); no senescence induction or senescent condition in the dataset, so no sample can be labelled senescent or a control of senescence.

No confirmation of senescence is stated in the series text. The treatment labels name the senescent conditions (8 days; 6 days for PBMCs). DMSO proliferating controls serve drug and IR conditions and empty-vector controls serve RasV12 in BJ and WI-38. HUVEC etoposide samples have a 50 µM description but a 10 µM treatment label.

Senescence is induced by ADAR1 knockdown in CaCO2 cancer cells; the fields give no marker of senescence (no SA-beta-gal etc.). Libraries are Input samples of a MeRIP-seq design, with 2 replicates per group.

No sample is described as senescent: cell-line samples are TGFβ 0 h/3 h (SASP gene expression) or MED15 phospho-mutants, and 6 samples are mouse hippocampus tissue. Labels are excluded, not senescent/control, because no senescent condition is defined.

No sample is stated to be senescent; the series only mentions therapy-induced senescence in general and the 40 h samples are for a death/replication-catastrophe comparison. 5-Ph-IAA (TIM degradation) alone may induce senescence but the fields do not say so.

SuperSeries of several sub-series covering many cell types, each with proliferating DMSO controls and etoposide, IR, doxorubicin, H2O2 or RasV12 inducers, all sampled at 6-8 days. The HUVEC etoposide samples give 50 µM in the description but 10 µM in the treatment field.

Only a TL1A knockdown versus non-targeting siRNA comparison in primary chondrocytes; no senescence induction or senescent condition is described in these fields, so no sample can be labelled senescent or as a control of senescent cells.

All samples are cartilage tissue from OA patients (smooth vs damaged areas, n=8 pairs); sample titles only say Medical/Lateral cartilage, not which is smooth or damaged. No senescence induction or senescent condition is described.

Senescence is induced by M1 THP-1 conditioned medium (inflamm-aging model), validated only by qPCR of M1 and aging genes. The ingredient-treated groups (bakuchiol, Terminalia chebula) are rescue perturbations and are excluded.

confirmation_stated: decreased senescence-associated (SA)-β-Gal activity with EGCG in etoposide-treated ECs
note: The sequenced cells are THP1 monocytes, not endothelial cells; senescence was induced (etoposide) only in the HUVECs co-cultured with them, so no sample is itself senescent. All samples were also LPS-stimulated for 2 h.

Senescence is stated only in the series title and summary (cisplatin- or CX-5461-induced senescence), with no confirmation assay. Each drug has its own vehicle control: saline for cisplatin, NaH2PO4 for CX-5461.

The fields never state that any sample is senescent; the title only suggests that passaged pancreatic endoderm cells without Y-27632 or other additives may become senescent. Samples are differentiation stages (iPSC, pancreatic endoderm, hPSC-β) and passaging conditions, so states are mostly unclear.

Samples are Tfh cells (CD4 T cells) taken from blood of control and aged individuals, not cultured cells and with no senescence induction; the summary only says aged Tfh show a senescence-like transcriptional program, so none is labelled senescent.

Series title mentions preventing senescence in passaged pancreatic endoderm cells, but the fields never state that any sample is senescent. Both samples are iPSC-derived pancreatic endoderm, so the labels are unclear.

All samples are senescent DKFZ-BT66 cells (oncogene-induced by KIAA1549::BRAF, doxycycline-OFF state); only the DMSO samples are labelled senescent, and the trametinib time points (15 min to 24 h) are excluded as MAPK-inhibition perturbations. The summary names no direct senescence assay.

Senescence is induced by mitomycin C in hTERT-immortalised ASC52telo adipose MSCs and collected after 10 days. The 2x2 design with GDF11 means the GDF11-treated samples (with or without MmC) are excluded as perturbations. The series text gives no senescence marker.

CTR are untreated parental cells; TIS are doxorubicin-treated cells (5 days drug, then 7 days, or 19 days for HFF, in fresh medium); REPOP are cells that regrew after TIS and are labelled excluded as escape from senescence. The fields name no assay confirming senescence.

confirmation_stated: Nuclear morphological analysis indicative of senescence in U251 cells (no specific marker assay named)
note: Only the U251 LOXL3-KD condition is described as senescent; U87MG LOXL3-KD is described as mitotic catastrophe and is excluded. The U87MG controls are labelled as plain controls, but no senescent U87MG condition exists.

Samples are a mix of mouse liver tissue (CDA-HFD, vehicle or DpC senolytic; no senescence induced in culture) and Huh7 cultures. Huh7 batch 2 (Veh/Dp44mT) is read as palbociclib-induced senescent cells treated with vehicle or the senolytic Dp44mT; batch 3 is Ctrl vs Palbo. The fields give no explicit palbociclib treatment for batch 2 and no senescence marker.

The overall design names both Week 1 and Week 4 etoposide samples as senescent, so both are labelled senescent. The summary says p16_variant 5 only became detectable at week 4, so week 1 cells may be less deeply senescent.
Only two samples (control and AMF30a, a PAD2 inhibitor); no senescence was induced in these samples, and the TGF-β senescence conditions mentioned in the summary are not in this dataset.

confirmation_stated: flow cytometry-based senescence assay detecting senescence in primary AML blasts after ex vivo chemotherapy
note: Primary patient AML blasts cultured ex vivo on feeders, paired untreated (nt) vs daunorubicin (tr, 5 days); 'cell line' is a patient code. Samples are labelled TIS_high or TIS_low by senescence capacity. Only TIS_high treated samples are called senescent; TIS_low pairs are unclear because the fields do not say senescence was reached.

No DOX-free control is in this dataset. DOX alone is taken as the senescent condition (TRF2DN-induced telomere dysfunction). DOX+CBP30 samples are excluded as a compound perturbation. The summary does not state a senescence marker.

Senescence is induced by dox-inducible TRF2DN in the iAT2 epithelial cells of the organoid. The profiled cells are the co-cultured fibroblasts (HFLFs) sorted out of the organoids, and the fields do not say that these fibroblasts are senescent, so all states are unclear.

DLD1 cancer cells with TRMT6/TRMT61A overexpression versus empty-vector control. The series does not say that any sample is senescent, so there is no senescent condition. Samples are technical lane duplicates of 2 biological replicates per group.

Senescence here is induced in CART cells by repeated antigen activation/rest cycles; the series says it is more prominent in 4-1BB than CD28 CART, so the D15 CD28 labels are the least certain. Day 8 CART samples are taken before the repeated activation and are treated as intermediate.

All samples are tBHP-treated for 4 days (stress phase); the series separates this stress phase from the later senescent phenotype, so no sample is clearly stated to be senescent. No untreated control is included; the controls are scrambled-shRNA samples.

All cells are palbociclib-induced senescent SKMel-103 melanoma cells; only vehicle samples are plain senescent, while StnI (senotoxin) time-course samples are excluded as senolytic treatment. Overall design says SKMel147 whereas sample fields say SKMel-103, and no duration of palbociclib treatment is given.

confirmation_stated: increased β-galactosidase activity; impaired proliferation, atypical cell cycle distribution, morphologically abnormal enlarged cells
note: Titles and characteristics (genotype/treatment) contradict each other for many samples, so the condition of 7 samples (GSM8819645, 647, 649, 650, 653, 658) cannot be decided and is unclear; senescence here is induced by doxycycline-induced HUWE1 shRNA knockdown (sh2 or sh3) in H358 cells.

Irradiated cells at day 5 (6 and 24 Gy) are labelled senescent because the series says irradiation induces senescence but names no time point, so the last one was taken. Day 1 irradiated samples are treated as intermediate. No specific senescence assay is named in the summary.

Human PSC27 stromal cells were laser-captured from PC3 xenograft tumours in mice, so they are not cultured cells. All 3 samples are MIT plus the senomorphic DMY, with no senescent or control arm in this message, so they are excluded.

Mixed design: IMR-90 ER:Ras oncogene-induced senescence (4-OHT 6 d) and TIG-3 etoposide-induced senescence with proliferating DMSO controls. IMR-90 OIS has no non-induced control; siRNA knockdown samples (p300/CBP, FOXF1/2, cJUN/JUNB/JUND) are excluded as perturbations. The shared 'cell type: senescent fibroblast' field also covers the TIG-3 proliferating controls.

THP-1 macrophages with ox-LDL alone vs ox-LDL+MLN4924 (48 h, foam cells); the series does not state that ox-LDL cells are senescent, so no clear senescent or control sample. MLN4924 samples are drug-perturbed.

Only the WT pair (pre-SnC vs SnC) serves as plain control and senescent samples; the Mito-Lyso linker samples are excluded as perturbed. Pre-senescent controls are described as low passage (<15-17) and are presumably not irradiated.
Human PBMCs from young and older donors before and after acute exercise; no senescence induction in culture and no senescent condition. Senescence appears only as a pathway enrichment term.

Arsenite toxicity study in hMSCs; no senescence was induced or confirmed, so there is no senescent condition. The two Agilent reference RNA samples are a commercial pool of 10 cell lines, not experimental cells.

Senescent and young states are defined only by passage (20th 'consider as senescent', 12th 'young'); no senescence marker is reported. D-ribose-treated samples at both passages are labelled excluded as perturbations; the 10 and 17 day times are culture times in 3D collagen, not times after an inducer.

HeLa Kyoto cervical cancer cells treated with docetaxel; the series only tests for a 'senescence-like' program and does not state that senescence was reached, so all samples are unclear. The cell type is listed as 'Endothelial cells' in the fields, which looks like a metadata error for a HeLa line.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal and γH2AX staining; SPiDER-βGal staining followed by flow cytometry
note: The series does not state the time point at which senescence was reached, and the UV and cisplatin doses and times are not given for most samples. Cisplatin and UV samples are labelled senescent from the series claim that DNA damage triggers senescence. The Day 6 UV sample is taken as the senescent time point of the UV time course. HC-iMC UV samples are labelled senescent as well, but the summary describes senescence only for XP melanocytes.

Human tendon biopsies (healthy hamstring vs chronic tendinopathic rotator cuff); no senescence induction in culture. Senescence is only discussed for the mouse part of the study, so no sample is senescent.

Myeloma cell lines with doxycycline-induced ID2 overexpression for 24 h; the summary links ID2 overexpression to cell-cycle arrest and senescence but does not say that senescence was reached at this 24 h time point, so ID2-OE and their WT controls are labelled unclear.

No senescent condition or senescence marker is stated; the series only mentions ERG's role in cell senescence. Overexpression of ERG or ΔIDR13 is not described as inducing senescence, so all samples are unclear.

confirmation_stated: Senescence assessed by immunostaining (in the summary; no specific marker named)
note: Senescence is induced in BT-40 cells by a 24 h drug pulse and 6 day wash-out. The series text says all three drugs induce senescence in vitro, so all drug samples are labelled senescent. Controls are DMSO vehicle, from two batches.

confirmation_stated: reduced proliferation; increased secretion of IL-6 and IL-8; impaired wound healing capacity
note: Replicative senescent HUVECs (>35 passages) and irradiated HUVECs (10 Gy, 10 day recovery) are both labelled senescent; controls are early passage cells. Technical triplicates.

Senescence is not induced by a classic inducer: HFS patient fibroblasts (ANTXR2 mutation) are described as showing senescence hallmarks. ANTXR2 siRNA samples are not stated to be senescent, so they and their siCTRL are unclear.

Senescence is induced by tau (MAPT) overexpression in the U87 glioma line, compared with empty-vector controls. The summary says tau induces senescence but gives no assay or time point, so the OE label rests on that statement.

Time course of Tet-on RASG12V induction in hTERT-immortalized fibroblasts; D10 taken as the senescent point since the series does not name one. Samples 7 and 8 (D10 with shGATAD2A and shJUN, labelled AA and WT) are knockdown conditions and are excluded.

Senescent time points are not named in the series; the last time point of each time course was taken (LS8817 Palbo day28, Doxo day21; MCF7 Palbo+Fulv day21) and earlier points are excluded as intermediate. LS8817 carries a TetON FLAG-MDM2 construct with no doxycycline stated.
Bulk RNA-seq of human prostate tissue (large vs small BPH prostates); no senescence was induced in culture, so no sample is a senescent or control sample.

Contains mouse liver tissue samples (young/aged, SIRT7 WT/KO; excluded as not cultured) and IMR90 cultures. Only the etoposide shSC IMR90 samples are plain senescent; NUCKS1 knockdown samples are excluded as perturbations (the study says NUCKS1 depletion delays senescence).

confirmation_stated: Proteomic profiling confirmed enrichment of neurodegeneration- and senescence-associated secretome signatures (HSV-1 infection)
note: Senescence is claimed only for HSV-1 infection of iPSC-derived cerebral organoids, supported by secretome and transcriptome signatures; TBEV-infected samples are labelled excluded because the series does not describe them as senescent. Exact collection time is not given per sample (up to 7 dpi).

confirmation_stated: Senescence assessed by immunostaining (markers not specified in summary)
note: All samples are GFP+ BT-40 cells FACS-sorted from orthotopic mouse xenograft brain tumours, not cultured cells; senescence was induced in vivo by trametinib (one week), so all samples are excluded as not cultured cells although the series describes the trametinib group as senescent and the vehicle group as the control.

confirmation_stated: p16-promoter driven GFP reporter expression, sorted by FACS (GFP+ = senescent, GFP- = non-senescent)
note: Senescence is defined by p16-promoter GFP reporter positivity after 10 days of LPS. The GFP- LPS-treated cells (SR) are the non-senescent, stress-resistant population, labelled not senescent. No SA-beta-gal or other independent assay is stated.

Samples are NGS libraries of extracellular RNA released into the culture medium of etoposide-treated osteosarcoma cells (dying or senescent), not RNA of the cells themselves. They were labelled excluded (other) because they do not represent the transcriptome of senescent cells; no cellular control is present.

confirmation_stated: reduced proliferation and increased secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and IL-8) in senescent and chronically inflamed cells; impaired wound healing
note: The series text describes replicative and radiation senescence, but this dataset holds only untreated and TNFα-treated (5h acute, 9d chronic) HUVECs. The series does not call the chronic TNFα cells senescent, so no sample has a senescent label.

The samples are donor monocyte-derived macrophages exposed to conditioned medium; the senescent cells (irradiated PTECs) were not sequenced, so no sample is senescent. Treated samples show the effect of senescent-cell secretome on macrophages, not senescence.

All 25 samples are control-donor iNSC lines (base, or treated with conditioned medium from PMS iNSCs, with or without senolytic); no PMS iNSC samples are in this dataset, and no sample is described as senescent. The summary claims senescence of PMS iNSCs only on transcript and single-cell evidence.

The series text never says that 4OHT-treated ER:RAS cells became senescent and gives no senescence assay, so siNT 4OHT samples and their DMSO controls are labelled unclear. Samples GSM8987297-300 are titled siNT2 but their treatment field says 'siNT1'; they are treated as siNT controls.

Acute 6 h auxin-inducible degron depletion in DLD1 cells; no senescent condition is in this dataset (senescence work is in other parts of the study), so all samples are excluded. DMSO samples are vehicle controls of depletion, not of senescence.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal staining (used to pre-identify senescent and non-senescent BPH epithelial cells)
note: All samples are primary BPH epithelial cells after 6 h co-culture with CD4+ T cells, so the profiles reflect T cell exposure. The inducer of senescence is not stated; library names of the non-senescent samples (PTE-TBHP) hint at TBHP but the fields do not explain this.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal staining of adjacent tissue sections
note: Cells were microdissected from frozen human BPH tissue (no in vitro culture); senescent vs non-senescent status comes from SA-β-gal staining of adjacent sections, not from an applied inducer.
Passage 5 vs passage 15 fibroblasts described as young vs old; the series never states that p15 cells are senescent and gives no senescence marker, so all samples are labelled unclear.

confirmation_stated: accumulation of SA-ßgal+ cells and morphological alterations
note: Irradiated samples (Si, Fe, H particles and gamma, 4 Gy) are labelled senescent as the series says 13 days of rest allowed senescence induction. Controls are shipped mock-irradiated cells and low-passage unshipped cells.

Cancer cell lines treated with an EZH2 PROTAC for 2 days. The summary says PROTAC-6272 induced senescence only in 'some' PCa cell lines and does not say whether VCaP or 22Rv1 is one of them, so the PROTAC samples and their controls are unclear. EPZ-6438 samples are a comparator drug arm.

The series never mentions senescence: HeLa cells were treated with olaparib for 72 h with moderate anti-proliferation and DNA damage, so the senescent state is not established. Both samples are labelled unclear.

The series states senescence was induced by doxorubicin or irradiation, but names no senescence marker; only mitochondrial staining is mentioned. ENRICH samples are doxorubicin-treated MCF7 re-seeded after 6 days and collected 24 h later (engulfing-enriched subpopulation), so they are labelled excluded rather than plain senescent.
KRT19 overexpression vs empty vector in A549 lung cancer cells; senescence is not induced or mentioned, so the dataset has no senescent condition.
KRT19 knockdown versus non-targeting shRNA in PC-9 lung cancer cells; no senescence is induced or studied, so no sample is senescent or a control of senescent samples.

Human healthy BM-MSCs were sorted after 42 h co-culture with non-CHIP, low-risk CHIP or high-risk CHIP HSPCs. The series text does not say that these human MSCs became senescent (senescence is described for the mouse model), so all samples are unclear.
LX-2 hepatic stellate cells treated with TGF-β with or without ligustilide; the series does not mention senescence and has no senescent or control condition, so all samples are excluded.

Tissue samples: microdissected human naevi and adjacent perilesional skin from patients. No senescence was induced and no senescence marker was reported, so no sample is labelled senescent or as a control.

The fields never say that any sample reached senescence and give no passage number or time point, so NC controls are unclear. The knockdown samples (siRNA/CRISPRi of SAMM50, CMKLR1, SERPING1) are excluded as perturbations. IL6+ and IL6- are treatment arms of the inflammatory screen.

Gastric cancer AGS cells with miR-214-3p overexpression or knockdown; no senescence induction or senescent condition, so senescence is only a gene-function term in the summary. All samples are excluded.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal activity increases across passages (P3-P33); p21/p53 upregulation and LMNB1 downregulation at RNA/protein levels
note: The series never names which passage is senescent; P33 is taken as senescent (last passage) and P24/P30 as intermediate. P11 is treated as the young control, also the parent of the DOX and DMSO samples. DOX duration is not stated.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal activity, LMNB1 expression and p21 levels (for the PURPL depletion in senescent cells)
note: The sample fields do not say whether the CRISPRi cells (sgCtrl, sgRNA-PURPL) were senescent or which inducer was used; the summary only says depletion was done in senescent cells. The OE/Ctrl pair is in young BJ fibroblasts, and the series does not state that overexpression reached full senescence.

No sample is explicitly called senescent: the summary says XRCC1-deficient cells show 'features of senescence', with no time point or marker given. XRCC1-KO is the only plausible senescent group and the Control-KO samples are its controls, so all samples are labelled unclear.

Blood T lymphocytes from healthy volunteers during simulated microgravity (dry immersion); no senescence is induced or studied, so there is no senescent condition. All samples are labelled excluded as not cultured cells.

Senescence was induced in the HT-1080 cancer cell line by dominant-negative TRF2 (telomere uncapping, 6 days). GNF7-treated senescent samples are excluded as senolytic-treated; DMSO-treated senescent samples are the senescent set, and cycling DMSO cells are the controls.

Cancer cell lines with BCAT1 knockdown; the summary only mentions ROS-induced senescence as a consequence of BCAT1 loss and states no senescent sample or confirmation assay. No sample is labelled senescent, and shCtrl samples are not stated to be proliferating.

Senescence is induced by CRISPR knockout of PP2Ac (series: it 'induces robust senescence'), so the WT cells are the controls. The D425 radiation (10 Gy) samples are unclear because the fields do not say that senescence was reached after RT. No senescence assay is named in the summary or design.

All samples are WI-38 fibroblasts with control or COPI-subunit siRNA at 72 h. The dataset has no senescent samples. The summary mentions proliferating and senescent cells, but the sample fields do not say which state these samples are in.

Senescence is induced by the KAT6A inhibitor WM1119 in PPP2R1A-mutant (R183W) HEC50B cells. The treatment duration is not stated, and the summary does not say whether CRISPR-WT cells treated with WM1119 become senescent, so those samples are unclear.

All four samples are vehicle (DMSO) tubuloids; no cisplatin-treated senescent samples are in this dataset, so there is no senescent condition. The summary mentions senescence markers after repeated cisplatin but names no specific measurement.

Senescence is induced by CRISPR knockout of NIT2 (summary: NIT2 knockout 'induced senescence'); NTC is a non-targeting guide control. GLS1-KO and NIT2-GLS1-KO are not described as senescent and are excluded as perturbations; no time after induction is stated (6 days of selection only).

HUVEC treated with the metabolite αKGM (4 h or 24 h) versus control; no senescence inducer was applied and no sample is described as senescent (senescence is only mentioned for NIT2 knockout, which is not in this dataset). All samples are therefore excluded.

Primary skin cells treated with antioxidants (chlorogenic acid, taurine) for 24 h; no senescence was induced and no senescent condition exists, so no sample can be labelled senescent or a control of senescent samples.

Stress granule study in U2OS cells (arsenite stress, RK-33 DDX3 inhibitor); no senescence is induced or measured, so no sample has a senescent condition. Soluble and insoluble are RNP granule fractionation fractions.

No sample is stated to be senescent: the series only says control 184D cells 'approached replicative senescence' at p17, so controls are labelled unclear. All other samples carry YAP1/MYC overexpression or are immortalised derivatives; p16sh was applied to all samples.

confirmation_stated: senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity (also ROS, p62 and autophagosome accumulation, G2/M cell cycle arrest) after OncoD-0J1 infection
note: This dataset only compares parental LN229 with sJAG1-expressing LN229; no senescence was induced in these samples (the senescence work in the series concerns oHSV-infected cells, not included here). Neither condition is shown to be senescent or a control of a senescent condition.

confirmation_stated: senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity; cell cycle analysis (G2/M arrest), increased ROS, p62 and autophagosome accumulation
note: Samples are primary GBM cells 48 h after oncolytic HSV infection; senescence is described for OncoD-0J1 in the summary, but not explicitly for the 48 h RNA-seq samples. The OncoD control virus is labelled unclear because the fields do not say whether it induces senescence.

Only wild-type vs calumenin knockout HFL1 fibroblasts, with no inducer and no sample described as senescent. The fields do not say that the KO cells are senescent, so no sample is labelled senescent or as a control.

Senescent state rests on the series description of IR-induced senescence at day 10; no senescence marker is stated. The non-targeting siRNA samples (called NT3/NT4 in titles, NT1/NT2 in the summary) are the senescent references; CCND1, CDK4, CDK6 and CDK4+6 knockdowns are excluded as perturbations.

Senescent+DMSO is the senescent condition; the palbociclib and ruxolitinib samples were treated on days 4-10 after IR and are excluded as perturbed. No senescence marker is reported in the series text.

All samples received high glucose; there is no untreated or normal-glucose control. Control-lentivirus + high glucose is taken as the senescent condition, and PDZK1-overexpressing cells are excluded as a perturbation. The text names no senescence marker measurement.

Senescence is induced by 48 h high glucose (37.5 mM) in ARPE-19 cells; the control medium has 5.5 mM glucose plus 32 mM mannitol as an osmotic control. The series text states that hyperglycemia induces senescence, but no senescence assay is named in the summary or design.

The sequenced cells are OVCAR8 bystander cells exposed to conditioned media (from cisplatin-senescent cells, SCM, or from proliferative cells, PCM), not senescent cells themselves. The dataset therefore holds no senescent sample, and all samples are labelled excluded.

Postmortem human brain tissue from AD patients and age-matched controls; no senescence induction in culture and no senescent condition defined, so none of the samples can be labelled senescent or as a control of one.

Gastric cancer AGS cells in complete medium vs 10 days of serum deprivation; senescence is never mentioned, so the dataset has no senescent condition and no sample is labelled as a senescent or control sample.
AML cell lines with CRISPRi MYBL2 knockdown versus non-targeting luciferase sgRNA; no senescence induction or senescent condition is described, so all samples are excluded.

Senescence is induced by the VCP inhibitor CB-5339 (7 days) in two cholangiocarcinoma lines, HuCCT1 and RBE. The summary states that the drug induces senescence but names no assay in the series text. The DMSO samples are vehicle controls.

Senescence is only inferred from RNA-seq (p53, SASP up; E2F/G2M down) and no named senescent time point, so the 14 d samples are taken as senescent as the last time point. The MMC dose differs between the shared protocol (0.3 mg/mL) and the sample fields (0.1 mg/mL).

Senescence is induced by shRNA knockdown of YTHDC1 in A2780 ovarian cancer cells (inducer labelled 'other'); the summary states knockdown promotes senescence but names no assay or time point, and the controls are shCtrl cells.

Senescent state is labelled for irradiated controls as the series' senescent condition; the time after irradiation of the control samples is not stated. CCCP-treated (Parkin mitochondrial clearance) and mtRNA-transfected samples are excluded as perturbations.

Includes CRISPR KO and siRNA knockdown cells (excluded as perturbations) and mouse liver samples from MASH animals (not cultured cells). Senescence in MRC5 was induced by 20 Gy X-ray, collected days 10-20; no senescence marker is stated in the series text.

confirmation_stated: impaired proliferation, diminished migratory capacity, upregulated senescence markers (p53, p21, p16)
note: Senescence is a disease-associated phenotype of patient-derived (BAV-TAA) iPSC-derived endothelial cells, with no inducer applied; controls are healthy-donor iECs. Source_name says aortic tissue, but the samples are iPSC-derived cells at passage 4.

P10 hAMSCs are described as a heterogeneous mix of aged and non-aged cells, and the fields do not say they are senescent, so the P10 controls are unclear. The PBL coculture removes aged cells and promotes proliferation, so it is excluded.
The RNA-seq samples are peripheral blood lymphocytes, not MSCs, with or without coculture with MSCs. The dataset has no senescent condition, so no sample is a senescent sample or a control of one.

Heat shock (44 C, 2 h) is treated as a perturbation, so all HS samples are excluded; only the NHS samples serve as senescent (doxorubicin, 10 days) or control (proliferating, contact-inhibited quiescent) labels. The summary does not state a senescence marker.

Senescence is induced by GDF15 knockdown in the KHM-5M thyroid cancer line; the summary says GDF15 depletion induces senescence but names no assay or time point, and the 'blank control' is untreated. Inducer is labelled 'other' (gene knockdown).
Senescence confirmation is not given in the series text; labels rely on sample titles (SENESCENT / NON SENESCENT). Tozasertib is an Aurora kinase inhibitor, labelled as inducer 'other'.

The fields give only passage numbers; the split into young (P3-6), pre-senescent (P14-16) and senescent (P22-26) is inferred from the title's three groups and the triplet structure, not stated per sample. No senescence marker is given.

Only pre-senescent colonic fibroblasts treated with siControl or siDUSP4 are described; no senescent condition or senescence confirmation is stated, so no sample can be labelled senescent or as a clear control.

Only wild-type (C1-2) iPSC-derived smooth muscle cells at 1 or 2 weeks of pulsatile flow; no progeria (LMNA HGPS) or other senescent condition is among these samples, so none can be labelled senescent or as a control.

iPSC-derived endothelial cells compared by APOE genotype (APOE33 vs APOE44), all untreated. No senescence inducer and no senescent or control condition is described in the fields, so all samples are labelled as having no senescent condition.

Despite the title, the dataset has no sample described as senescent: it compares APOE44 and APOE33 iPSC-derived endothelial cells with and without 24 h cytokine treatment. All samples are labelled excluded because there is no senescent condition.

iPSC-derived vascular cells in 3D hydrogel (APOE genotype not given in sample fields); the series is about APOE4-driven endothelial senescence but no senescence induction or senescent condition is defined for this sample.

The title mentions APOE4-driven endothelial senescence, but the fields give no senescence inducer, no senescent condition and no senescence assay; samples compare APOE33/APOE44 iPSC-ECs, with or without cytokines (IFNg, TNFa, IL1b), plus one 3D vascular culture pool. All samples are labelled excluded (no senescent condition).

Inducer is inferred from sample titles (OIS = oncogene-induced senescence); the series text does not name the oncogene or time point. ALKBH8 knockdown and ALKBH8-SM-1 samples are excluded as perturbations in both OIS and proliferating cells.

Replicative senescence time course in WI-38 by population doubling level (PDL). The series does not name the senescent PDL, so the last point (PDL 57) is taken as senescent and PDL 21 as young control; middle PDLs are treated as intermediate. No senescence marker is stated in the series text.
WI-38 replicative-aging series (PDL 21 to 57). The text does not say which passages are senescent, so every sample is labelled unclear. PDL 21 is probably the young control.

confirmation_stated: Morphology, growth kinetics, and confluence were monitored (no specific senescence marker named)
note: Cells were passaged until replicative senescence or passage 10, and the fields never say which donors reached senescence, so the last passages are not confirmed senescent. Every sample is therefore labelled unclear, including the early passages.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal positivity (late, lysosome-dependent SA-β-gal-positive states) and DDR activation
note: The series does not name which time point is senescent; day 7 treated samples were labelled senescent (last time point) and day 3 treated samples as intermediate. Samples come from two environments (AGL aboveground vs DUL underground); alisertib is an Aurora A inhibitor (mitotic insult).

confirmation_stated: SA-ßGal staining and FACS isolation of SA-ßGal-low and SA-ßGal-high CD8+ T cells
note: Primary CD8+ T cells from peripheral blood, freshly sorted by SA-ßGal level without culture; senescence is naturally occurring (no inducer). SA-ßGal-high is treated as senescent and SA-ßGal-low as the non-senescent control in both young and old donors.

Senescence is only claimed in the series title (miP-FERMT3 induces p53-mediated arrest and senescence); the summary and design give no senescence measurement. miP-100 solvent samples are labelled senescent from the title alone, and the IL-1β arms are treated as extra perturbations.

confirmation_stated: SA-ßGal staining (SA-ßGal-high vs SA-ßGal-low cells sorted by FACS)
note: The 'treatment' characteristic is shifted by one position relative to the title and library name (e.g. title CADD522 carries treatment DMSO); labels follow the title/library name, which agree with each other. Senescent cells are primary CD8+ T cells sorted by SA-ßGal and then cultured 3 days with IL2; inhibitor-treated samples are excluded as perturbations.

confirmation_stated: SA-ßGal staining (SA-ßGal-high vs SA-ßGal-low cells isolated by FACS)
note: Senescent (SA-ßGal-high) and non-senescent (SA-ßGal-low) CD8+ T cells were sorted from blood, not induced in culture. All TF-siRNA samples and all anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulated samples are excluded as perturbations; only unstimulated scramble samples are plain senescent/control.

Six samples are HUVEC cells (senescent vs early passage); six are RNA from extracellular vesicles secreted by those cells, labelled excluded because they are not cells. No senescence marker assay is stated in the series text.
Half of the samples are RNA from extracellular vesicles released by HUVECs, not cells; they are labelled excluded (other). No senescence confirmation assay is given in the SuperSeries text.

Cytotoxicity study of cinnamon essential oil (4 h) versus DMSO in HaCaT, HeLa and SiHa cells; no senescence was induced or measured, so no sample is senescent and none is stated to be proliferating or quiescent.

No sample is described as senescent: the study induces senescence by ZNF865 knockdown, which is not in this dataset (only CRISPRa ZNF865 upregulation, NTC controls, healthy and degenerative NP cells). All samples are therefore labelled excluded with the reason 'no senescent condition in the dataset'.

The series text is only a SuperSeries stub and no sample is described as senescent or as proliferating or quiescent, so all samples are labelled excluded for lack of a senescent condition. The samples are ASC, HEK293 and primary nucleus pulposus cells with or without CRISPRa ZNF865 (dCas9-VPR).

The 'cell type' and 'cell line' characteristics are mislabeled (cell type holds condition labels such as WT, TRF2DN; cell line holds 'endothelial cell'). Premature senescence is driven by TRF2 dominant-negative (telomere uncapping), labelled inducer 'other'.

Senescence is inferred only from RNA-seq GSEA (SASP, NF-κB, p53 signalling) after PTPA re-expression in ZL34 cells. No senescence assay such as SA-beta-gal is stated, so the senescent label rests on the series text alone.

Aged samples are keratinocytes from 77- and 79-year-old donors, and the fields do not state that they are senescent. S100A7 knockdown is said to induce 'senescence markers', but no senescent state is stated, so all samples are unclear. Young donor cells are controls of unclear samples.

Senescence is only implied by the summary (oxidative stress/RLIM upregulation 'induced cellular senescence'); the time after H2O2 is not stated and no senescence marker is given for the RNA-seq samples.

Senescence is induced by the EGLN2 inhibitor A10P3C in the MDA-MB-231 cancer cell line, and the summary does not give the time point at which senescence was confirmed; the RNA-seq time point is 36 h. The treated samples are labelled senescent on the strength of the summary's general claim, and no senescence assay is named.

Both samples are doxorubicin-induced senescent TIG-3 cells; the ARV825 sample is a senolytic treatment (cells eliminated) and is excluded, while the DMSO sample is the senescent reference. No non-senescent control is present.

The series is mainly a gingival tissue single-cell study; these 6 samples are cultured fibroblasts with IFT88 knockdown vs control. The fields do not say whether the controls are aged or senescent, so they are unclear. The 'cell line' field holds 'shIFT88', which is a construct and not a cell line.

Factorial design (quiescent vs doxorubicin-senescent IMR-90, mock vs IAV, with or without acetate); only the mock, no-acetate samples are plain senescent or control, the rest are excluded as perturbations. No senescence marker is stated in the series text, and the time after doxorubicin is not given.

All samples are doxorubicin-induced senescent TIG-3 cells; DMSO samples are the untreated senescent reference, while ABT263/ARV825 samples are the surviving cells after senolytic treatment and are excluded. No proliferating control is included.

The series refers to a SASP phenotype after 8 or 12 Gy but does not state that senescence was confirmed, so irradiated and 0 Gy samples without drug are labelled unclear. All ADS-032 treated samples are excluded because the inflammasome inhibitor is an added perturbation.
All samples are PC3 xenograft tumors from mice (in vivo), not cultured cells. The summary is missing and no senescence marker is given, so palbociclib-treated tumors are not shown to be senescent.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal activity and γH2AX (summary, for AhR regulation of senescence in vitro and in vivo)
note: All samples are HBE cells treated for 24 h with cockroach allergen extract (CRE), with or without the AhR agonist VAF347. There is no untreated control, and the fields do not say that the CRE-treated HBE cells reached senescence, so the CRE-only samples are unclear.

The series never states that expanded CMs (CHIR99021 expansion) reached senescence, only that PAPD5 inhibitors were used to prevent it, so E-CM and N-CM are labelled unclear. Drug-treated groups (BCH001, RG7834) are excluded as perturbations.

Only the ZBH01 samples are described by the series as senescence-inducing; CPT11 and SN38 are comparator drugs for which the fields do not say senescence was reached. No dose or treatment duration is given, and the summary names no senescence assay for this RNA-seq experiment.

Four conditions (Ctrl, BIBR1532, Ctrl+Etoposide, BIBR1532+Etoposide); the series names only BIBR1532 followed by etoposide as the senescence induction, so BIBR1532 alone and Ctrl+Etoposide are labelled excluded. No senescence marker is stated in the series text.

confirmation_stated: SA-β-gal activity and protein levels of p53, p21 and γ-H2A.X (stated for Cisplatin-induced AKI kidneys; not stated specifically for the HK-2 RNA-seq samples)
note: All six samples are cisplatin-treated HK-2 cells, with no untreated control. The siNC samples are labelled senescent as the cisplatin senescent condition, and the NAT10 knockdown samples are excluded as perturbed. Cisplatin exposure time is not stated.
Design is passage 3 vs passage 7 ADSCs. The text speaks of senescent ADSCs but never says that P7 is the senescent state or how senescence was confirmed, so both groups are labelled unclear.

All samples were harvested after only 24 h of 4 nM doxorubicin, whereas the series says senescence arises after prolonged low-dose treatment, so no sample is labelled senescent. Untreated sgNTC samples are controls only in name. TDP2-KO and peposertib samples are perturbations.

confirmation_stated: p53/p21 activation and increased genomic instability (summary)
note: No senescence inducer was applied. The study compares SLF2-mutant iPSC-derived HSPCs with gene-corrected isogenic controls, and senescence is only mentioned as a transcriptional signature in mutants, so the state is unclear for all samples.

confirmation_stated: miR-205-5p induces the senescence marker β-galactosidase in lung ECs
note: Senescence here is induced by miR-205-5p mimic transfection (not a classical inducer); the summary gives only β-galactosidase as evidence, so the senescent label is a moderate-confidence call. Controls received a negative control mimic.

The series does not mention senescence. It studies dox-inducible PRCC-TFE3 expression and CDK8/19 inhibition in HK-2 cells, so no sample has a senescent condition. All samples are excluded, and none is labelled as proliferating or quiescent.

The fields describe only a comparison of control and NFIC knockout U2OS cells, with no inducer and no stated senescent condition. SIRT6 knockdown vs wild-type in G361 melanoma cancer cells; senescence is only mentioned as a pathway altered by SIRT6 inhibition, and no sample is stated to be senescent or proliferating.

THP-1-derived M0 macrophages were exposed to inert beads or to fragments shed by senescent cells (SCAFs); the macrophages themselves are not senescent, so no sample is a senescent or control state for senescence.

SIRT6 knockdown vs wild-type A375 melanoma cells; the series mentions senescence only as a pathway altered by SIRT6 inhibition and does not state that any sample is senescent, so no senescent condition is defined.

Snail1 induction suppresses proliferation, but the series does not state that senescence was reached (it says Snail1 blocks senescence via CEBPg/LaminB1), so Snail1 and vehicle samples are unclear. Cumate+Dox samples add an AR knockdown. Time points are 4 or 6 days of treatment after 2 days cumate pretreatment.

Sample titles and treatment fields conflict: titles H_I1-3 (likely H2O2 + IsoL) carry treatment 'H2O2', while titles H2O21-3 carry treatment 'Isoliensinine'. It is unclear which group is H2O2 alone (senescent) and which is H2O2 plus isoliensinine (perturbed), so all six are labelled unclear.

Human PBMC-derived macrophages, 3 donors, each with a mock-treated passage control, doxorubicin and irradiation senescence. The growth_protocol text describes mouse BMDMs, but the samples are human. Senescent samples were collected 10-13 days after DNA damage.

Only the Sen(IR) samples are plain senescent; all CCCP (mitochondria-depleted) samples with or without acetate and/or mtDNA are perturbed and excluded. No time after irradiation is stated, and no senescence marker is given in the series text.

Cancer cell line MDA-MB-231 with RNASEH2A knockout versus control vector; no senescence was induced and no sample is described as senescent or proliferating, so no sample can be labelled senescent or a control.

Senescence is stated for crizotinib treatment in the summary (alongside apoptosis and necroptosis in the combination), but the fields give no senescence marker. Controls are labelled only 'Control' (vehicle presumed).
Only the S group is the senescent condition (inducer not named in the fields); S+C and S+C+I are C3N QD treated (senolytic/photoactivated) and excluded. The dataset has no non-senescent control.

No senescence was induced in any sample: the series compares trisomy 21 with euploid NPCs and iPSCs, and the fields do not say that any sample is senescent. The iPSC libraries appear twice (E250027119 and E250027128) with identical sample codes, so they look like re-sequenced duplicates.

confirmation_stated: elevated SA-β-galactosidase activity, nuclear enlargement, increased p53 expression
note: hTERT-immortalised HCAECs from different donors; 10 Gy X-ray at day 7 is taken as senescent. Rapamycin-treated samples (alone or after IR) are excluded as perturbations. The 23 samples include donors with no IR-only sample, such as 17YO female.

Senescence is only asserted in the summary (lactating serum leads to senescence in PAPP-A+ MCF7 cells) with no stated confirmation assay. The 3D cultures are cultured cells; the xenograft tumours are tissue from mice and are excluded.

All samples are from the 'Sen Low' cohort, i.e. patient AML blasts that did not become senescent after chemotherapy; no senescent condition is in this dataset. Tazemetostat (PRC2/EZH2 inhibitor) samples are perturbations. Samples are assumed to be ex vivo cultured blasts, but this is not stated directly.
HPNE-hTERT is an hTERT-immortalized non-malignant line. The series says FOLFIRINOX induces senescence, but it gives no senescence assay. Senescence is taken from the treatment_protocol field.
Dataset is human skin biopsies (PKDL lesions vs healthy skin) with no senescence induction or senescent condition; unrelated to cellular senescence.

Dataset compares untreated RD rhabdomyosarcoma cells with vincristine-resistant derivatives; no senescence was induced or confirmed in these samples (senescence is only described for trametinib-treated resistant cells, which are not in this dataset).

confirmation_stated: SA-β-Gal-positive cells reduced; EdU incorporation assays showed enhanced proliferation after treatment
note: No sample is stated to be senescent or proliferating; P12 untreated and EGFP samples are late-passage hMSCs whose senescent state is not stated, and the protein-treated sample is a perturbation meant to counteract senescence.

Cancer cell line (MSTO-211H) in a 2x2 design of radiation (4 Gy) and quetiapine; the summary only says combined treatment increased senescence by sequencing, with no senescence assay. Irradiated and control samples are therefore labelled unclear.

Primary human blood neutrophils treated ex vivo with LPS, which the series calls 'senescence'. Neutrophils are short-lived, so this may not be the same as senescence in proliferating cells. No time point or confirmatory assay is given.

Senescence here is induced by MTR4 shRNA knockdown in young HUVECs; the summary states knockdown induces premature senescence, but this dataset's fields give no marker measurement or time point. shCtrl samples are the shRNA controls.

Senescence is induced with bleomycin; the summary and design name no senescence marker measurement. Ruxolitinib-treated samples (B_R) are excluded as a drug perturbation; the Bleo samples received vehicle after the 5-day post-induction point.

All samples are CD34+ bone marrow cells from MDS patients in a clinical trial (screening, post-cycle 2, post-cycle 4), not cultured cells. No senescence was induced in culture, and senescence is only discussed as an inflammatory program in short-term survivors.

confirmation_stated: senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining, western blot for p21 and p16
note: No inducer or senescent condition is described; the comparison is NAT10 overexpression versus wild-type ADSCs, so no sample is labelled senescent or as a control of a senescent sample.

The series only says DYRK1B overexpression promotes 'senescence-like' programs and names no senescent condition or senescence assay, so all samples are labelled unclear. The Y273F lines are the mutant counterpart of the WT DYRK1B lines.

Design has four groups: non-irradiated HDF, non-irradiated HDF with C3 siRNA, irradiated (IR) HDF, and IR-HDF with C3 siRNA. The C3 siRNA groups are labelled excluded as perturbations. No time after irradiation or senescence marker is stated.

SS is read as serum starved and FS as full serum; the 240h irradiated full-serum samples are labelled senescent, and untimed FS_IR samples are unclear. Bleomycin samples (not part of the primary analysis) are unclear because the fields do not say senescence was reached; no senescence marker assay is stated.

Only a part (112 of 192) of a SuperSeries is shown; the text does not say which IR time point is senescent, so the last one (240h) is taken as senescent. Bleomycin samples and untimed FS_IR samples are unclear, and serum-starved (SS) irradiated samples are excluded as a confounded condition.

The text does not say which tool compound gives senescence and which gives quiescence. Bleomycin and palbociclib are labelled senescent as chemically induced senescence inducers, and rapamycin and nocodazole are labelled unclear. Late-passage (LP) cells are labelled senescent as the stated healthy senescence control. All samples with navitoclax are excluded as senolytic.

IR samples at 8, 24 and 48 h are intermediate time points. CTL samples at 0 and 336 h are non-irradiated controls. The scRNA-seq extension described in the summary is not part of these samples.

confirmation_stated: Upregulation of p16 and p21 (in vitro proteomic analyses of PCS-exposed CD4+ T cells); cell-cycle arrest
note: The series does not name any sample group as senescent; PCS is said to induce senescence-associated programs in activated CD4+ T cells. Proliferating (CTV low) sorted samples are labelled not senescent, and the non-proliferating and PCS-treated non-proliferating samples are left unclear.

Circadian time-course of iPSC-derived OPCs from healthy controls and RRMS/SPMS patients; no senescence induction or senescent condition is described, so no sample can be labelled senescent or as a control. Some samples are titled 'excluded from analysis' by the submitters.

The sequenced cells are EA.hy926 endothelial cells exposed to young or mitomycin-C-senescent MSCs, not senescent cells themselves. No sample is senescent, so all are excluded; the MSCs were not sequenced, and the series states no senescence assay.

Lines carry LRRK2-G2019S, or are healthy or gene-corrected.

Replicative senescence of UC-MSCs by passage; only P12 is called senescent (late senescence), P2 is the early-passage control. P8 ('early senescence') and P10 ('intermediate') are labelled excluded as intermediate time points, and no senescence marker assay is stated.
HK-2 cells treated with 150 µM H2O2 for 48 h; the series says H2O2 triggers senescence but gives no time point or assay for it. YAP1-knockdown samples with H2O2 are excluded as perturbations.

The text mentions replicative senescence during MSC expansion but does not say P25 cells were confirmed senescent, so P25 and its P10 control are labelled unclear. The circ-OSK samples are rejuvenated P25 cells (reversal).

Senescence was induced by 15 Gy irradiation (10 days); controls are serum-starved quiescent cells. IAV-infected samples (24 h, MOI 1) are labelled excluded as an added perturbation. Mock-infected SEN and QUI samples are the plain senescent and control samples.

Matrin-3 knockdown in HCAECs with no senescence inducer. The series only says that pathways related to senescence were enriched, and it gives no senescence measurement for these cells. The samples are not labelled senescent.
Aged (passage 12) HUVECs are called replicatively senescent in the summary, but no senescence marker is given. GLUT3-overexpressing aged samples are excluded as perturbed.

Only DMSO-treated OIS (senescent) and DMSO-treated proliferating samples are plain; all SBI-0802162, FK866 and NR treated samples are drug perturbations. FK866 titles say 10uM but the treatment field says 0.01uM; the message lists 20 of 21 samples.

iPSC-derived neurons (DIV49) compared by APOE genotype (apoE3 vs apoE4); no senescence induction or senescent condition is described, only a mention of a senescence-like stress state in longitudinal proteomics, which is not part of this RNA-seq set.

No sample is described as senescent: the series is about engineering T cells to overcome replicative senescence, and no senescence marker is stated. ATP6AP1 siRNA knockdown vs non-targeting siRNA in LX-2 cells. The series only mentions senescence as a pathway of interest and does not say that senescence was induced or confirmed, so no sample is labelled senescent.

confirmation_stated: senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining; increased p21, p27, p57; reduced RB phosphorylation and SKP2; suppressed proliferation (high-dose 5β-DHT)
note: Senescence is described only for high-dose (100 nM) 5β-DHT, without naming the RNA-seq time point; the last point (72 h) is labelled senescent and 24 h as intermediate. HepG2 cancer cells treated with the UGCG inhibitor eliglustat; senescence is not induced or confirmed, only 'senescence-associated pathways' are enriched in the transcriptome at 30 µM. No sample is labelled senescent.

All samples are laser-capture microdissected FFPE human skin tissue (normal, nevus, melanoma; stroma, epidermis, tumour). No senescence induction or senescent condition is described, so all are excluded as not cultured cells.

All samples are IMR-90 taken 24 h after doxycycline-induced expression or after DMSO/antimycin A. The fields never say that senescence was reached at this time point, so every state is unclear.
